messages:
Maya: quick sync — strategic EU customer asked for GA-ready commitment: SLA, per-route token billing, and a 24/7 emergency support window. We need product+eng+sales alignment today.

Devin: can you share their latency targets and typical seq len? also peak QPS and regions?

Maya: targets: p95 < 150ms for 512 tokens, p99 < 300ms. Typical steady qps ~180, bursts up to ~1k for 3–5 min. Primary region EU with US fallback. Models: M-family (lm-v2) and a quantized variant.

Sam: TL;DR: Dedicated pinned pools + multi-AZ routing can meet 99.95% availability and tail latency. Shared hosted pools will need reserved burst capacity + fallback to quantized variants — higher tail risk.

Taylor: pricing: per-route token billing + 24/7 support implies a premium SKU or SLA surcharge. Need finops to model. Is customer ok with an addon?

Priya: commercial context — pilot ~$300k ARR Y1, strategic for EU expansion. They want concise SLA bullets to put in the MSA. High chance to convert.

Kelly: legal needs exact SLA metric definitions, credit formulas, and exclusions (maintenance, customer misconfig). Also define what constitutes an incident vs degradation.

Devin: monitoring & ops: propose per-route dashboards (p50/p95/p99), SLO burn-rate alerts, and an auto-rollback rule: if p95 > target for >5m, trigger failover and page oncall. Also want sampled request+response snapshots for quality drift.

Sam: engineering checklist (short):
- confirm model versions + seq length histogram
- infra plan for dedicated pinned pools, autoscale and burst handling
- fallback map: primary -> quantized -> smaller model (document quality deltas)
- synthetic load tests, staging soak, pilot shadowing
- oncall playbook & escalation matrix

Maya: docs: onboarding guide for customer SREs, runbook with escalation steps, expected behavior table (fallthrough quality notes), billing examples per-route. Target: docs sprint after scope finalization (1 week).

Taylor: tradeoff note — prioritizing this pilot shifts Optimize roadmap ~2 sprints. Is the revenue justification sufficient?

Priya: yes — commercial will push. Customer expects a pilot with exit criteria; they accept limited pilot capacity.

Sam: rough eng estimate: infra + routing + autoscale + fallback -> 3–4w (2 infra engs + 1 runtime). SLA testing and soak -> 1w. Docs/legal in parallel -> 1w. End-to-end ~5 weeks with parallel work.

Maya: propose two offers to present to customer:
A) Dedicated Pilot: 99.9% availability SLA (contracted), per-route token billing, 24/7 emergency support (pager + phone), contractual SLA credits, faster launch (~5w).
B) Hosted Pilot: conservative SLA 99.5%, burst addon for reserved capacity, limited emergency support (business hours + on-call), longer validation (~8w).

Kelly: legal asks to see the SLA credit formula and exclusions upfront. We'll not accept unlimited credits; include force majeure and scheduled maintenance windows.

Devin: ops guardrails: require traffic ramp plan (48h), approved test harness, and a rollback trigger: p99 > target for 10m sustained -> failover + page. Also require customer to share sample payloads and seq histogram before synthetic tests.

Sam: testing plan outline: 1) lab latency profiling across seq lens, 2) staging soak with prod-like traffic, 3) pilot shadowing with small % of traffic, 4) guarded cutover ramp. Need sample traces by EOD to start spike.

Maya: decision ask — team vote for A (Dedicated pilot) or B (Hosted pilot)? Please react.

Taylor: vote A if revenue is real
Devin: A
Kelly: A, legal will prep clauses once SLA numbers finalized
Priya: A, sales will draft contract skeleton and confirm customer signoff on pilot constraints

ops-bot: ticket created: PILOT-9123 "EU enterprise pilot SLA & per-route pricing" assigned to @Sam, @Devin, @Taylor

Sam: I'll open an infra spike for pinned pools and post initial latency profiles here. Need model version + payload samples.

Devin: I'll sketch per-route dashboard mock and alert thresholds; will include SLO burn-rate alarms and auto-escalation steps.

Taylor: I'll model pricing options (premium SKU vs addon surcharge) and run a quick rev/COGS delta for both offers.

Maya: owners + immediate actions: Maya (spec & docs), Sam (infra + tests), Devin (monitoring & rollback), Taylor (pricing scenarios), Priya (sales + contract), Kelly (legal review). Target spec draft in 48 hours.

Kelly: legal note — include explicit exclusion for customer-made misconfig and test-induced load during pilot; define scheduled maintenance notice window.

Maya: closing — if we pick A, call out limited pilot capacity, clear exit criteria, and a timeline for ramp to GA. Will coordinate and post spec in 48h. :white_check_mark:

Priya: customer already ok with an exit clause, will confirm exact wording.

Maya: thanks all — reconvene after the spec. :thumbsup:
